terms.grammar: adjective, third declension; with the dative or ad
evidence: Phaedr. 4.13.1: ūtilius hominī nihil est quam rēctē loquī
terms.comment: What it is useful for goes in the dative (tergendīs mēnsīs, for wiping tables) or with ad. The opposite is inūtilis.

terms.gloss: to be useful, to come in handy
terms.grammar: phrase: ūsus in the dative of purpose, often with magnō, and a dative of the person
evidence: Cic. Att. 1.1.3: fuit et mihi et Quīntō frātrī magnō ūsuī (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 5.1: ea quae sunt ūsuī ad armandās nāvēs (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: sum cocleīs habilis, sed nec minus ūtilis ōvīs. numquid scīs, potius cūr cocleāre vocer?
phrases.english: I am handy for snails, but no less useful for eggs. Do you know why I am called after the snail rather than the egg?

phrases.latin: nisi ūtile est quod facimus, stulta est glōria
phrases.english: unless what we do is useful, the glory is foolish
This will come in handy for you.

sources: Lewis & Short: utilis · Lewis & Short: inutilis · Lewis & Short: usus
